# BPCS Interlock Definition Sheet (IDS): Template and Worked Example

## How the template keeps setpoints in one place

Each sheet describes the interlock's logic and behavior, but no setpoint values.

1. **Store every number in one register.** Trip setpoints, reset thresholds, deadbands, timers and travel times live only in a single controlled register. This can be your instrument database, an alarm and trip register, or a dedicated table. The sheet refers to each value by its register ID, such as `SPR-1105-LL`.
2. **Configure from the register.** The configurer bulk-imports or keys values from the register, not from the sheet. The sheet tells them *which* parameter goes *where*.
3. **Pull values at test time.** FAT and SAT test sheets show "Expected: trip at SP(`SPR-1105-LL`)". The tester prints the register extract at its current revision and records it on the test record. The FAT then checks configured value against register value, which is the check you actually want.
4. **Change values only in the register, under MOC.** A setpoint change touches one record. The IDS only changes when logic or behavior changes.
5. **Allow one exception.** The legacy section may quote old values as historical evidence, clearly labeled as such.

---

## TEMPLATE

```
BPCS INTERLOCK DEFINITION SHEET
================================================================
IDS No.:            IDS-<unit>-<seq>          Revision: <A/B/0/1>
Title:              <short functional name>
Unit / Equipment:   <unit no.> / <equipment tag>
P&ID(s):            <drawing no. / rev>
New DCS controller: <controller / area>       Legacy: <old DCS node>
Status:             Draft / Reviewed / Approved for Config / FAT'd / SAT'd
================================================================
```

### 1. Classification and boundary
| Item | Entry |
|---|---|
| Interlock type | Process trip / Equipment protection / Permissive / Sequence step |
| Confirmed **not** a SIF (SRS doc & rev checked) | Y / N, ref: |
| Part of BMS / covered by burner-management standard? | Y / N, ref: |
| Credited as IPL in LOPA/HAZOP? | Y / N. If Y: scenario ref, and note BPCS IPL independence constraints |
| Shares sensor or final element with a SIF? | Y / N. If Y: tag(s), SIF no., and how independence is handled |
| Related interlocks / SIFs | |

### 2. Purpose
One or two sentences: the hazard or consequence prevented, and the action taken.

| Legacy logic reference (printout / sheet / block) | |
| Legacy C&E drawing reference | |
| Legacy values (historical, **not for configuration**) | |
| Discrepancies found (logic vs C&E vs field) | |
| Intentional changes in migration (with MOC no.) | |

- **Boolean expression:**
- **Latching:** Latched until manual reset / Self-resetting

### 6. Effects (outputs)

Cover bad PV, I/O card failure, controller failover behavior, and loss of comms to peer controllers.

## WORKED EXAMPLE

> The register values shown at the end are **illustrative only**, there to show what the register row looks like. In practice, the sheet carries only the IDs.

```
BPCS INTERLOCK DEFINITION SHEET
================================================================
IDS No.:            IDS-11-007                Revision: A
Title:              H-110 Low Fuel Gas Pressure – Close Main Fuel Valve
Unit / Equipment:   Unit 11 / H-110 Crude Heater
P&ID(s):            11-PID-004 rev 7
New DCS controller: CTL-11A                   Legacy: Node 3, Box 12
Status:             Draft
================================================================
```

### 1. Classification and boundary
| Item | Entry |
|---|---|
| Interlock type | Process trip |
| Confirmed not a SIF | **To confirm.** Check SRS rev __ for any heater fuel-gas low-pressure SIF |
| Part of BMS? | **To confirm.** See note after the example. |
| Credited as IPL? | N (HAZOP node 11-04, to confirm) |
| Shares sensor/final element with a SIF? | **To confirm** for XV-1106 |
| Related | IDS-11-008 (H-110 pilot gas low pressure), IDS-11-010 (heater trip summary) |

### 2. Purpose
Low fuel gas pressure at the burners can cause flame instability and flame-out, followed by accumulation of unburnt fuel in the firebox. This interlock closes main fuel gas shut-off valve XV-1106 on sustained low pressure.

### 3. Legacy traceability
| Item | Entry |
|---|---|
| Legacy logic ref | Node 3 logic printout, sheet 41, blocks LB-212 to LB-215 |
| Legacy C&E | 11-CE-002 rev 3, row 14 |
| Legacy values (historical only) | C&E shows trip at "0.35 barg"; logic block configured 0.30 barg; delay 2 s in logic, not shown on C&E |
| Discrepancies | Setpoint differs between C&E and logic. Bad-PV action is not documented on the C&E; the logic trips on bad PV. |
| Migration changes | None intended. Setpoint to be resolved via register (OI-1). |

### 4. Causes
| # | Tag | Description | Signal | Trip condition | Setpoint ref | Delay ref | Voting | Bad-quality action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | PT-1105 | H-110 fuel gas pressure downstream of PCV-1105 | 4–20 mA HART, AI card CTL-11A | PV < LL | `SPR-1105-LL` | `TMR-1105-LL` | 1oo1 | Trip, same as legacy (confirm, OI-2) |

### 5. Logic
- **Plain-language statement:** IF PT-1105 is below the LL setpoint, or bad quality, continuously for the LL delay, AND neither the startup override nor the maintenance bypass is active, THEN close XV-1106 and latch.
- **Boolean expression:** `TRIP = ((PT1105.PV < SP_LL) OR PT1105.BAD) · TON(TMR_LL) · NOT(SUO_ACTIVE) · NOT(BYP_ACTIVE)`
- **Latching:** Latched until manual reset.
- **First-out group:** H-110 heater trips (FO-11-H110).
- **Execution:** Same controller and task as XV-1106 output; scan class 250 ms or faster.

### 6. Effects
| # | Tag | Action on trip | De-energize to trip | Operator mode | Feedback | Discrepancy |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | XV-1106 | Close | Yes (SOV de-energize) | HMI open command blocked while tripped. Command forced to CLOSE. | ZSC-1106 / ZSO-1106 | Alarm if ZSC not made within `TMR-1106-TRV` |
| E2 | FV-1107 (fuel gas flow control) | Output to `SPR-1107-MINOP`, loop to MAN | n/a | Forced MAN | n/a | n/a |

E2 is shown as typical. Confirm against the legacy logic (OI-3).

### 7. Reset and restart
| Item | Entry |
|---|---|
| Reset type | Manual, HMI button on H-110 graphic |
| Reset permitted when | PT-1105 is good quality and above `SPR-1105-RST`. XV-1106 open command is in CLOSE. |
| Privilege | Operator |
| Effect of reset | Re-enables operator control only. XV-1106 stays closed until the operator opens it through the light-off sequence. |

### 8. Startup override
| Item | Entry |
|---|---|
| Required | Yes. Pressure is low by definition while XV-1106 is closed. |
| Trigger | Operator OPEN command on XV-1106 after reset |
| Duration | `TMR-1105-SUO` |
| Auto-cancel | Timer expiry, or PT-1105 above `SPR-1105-RST` (whichever comes first) |

### 9. Maintenance bypass
| Item | Entry |
|---|---|
| Permitted | Yes, for transmitter maintenance only |
| Mechanism | HMI bypass switch, engineer-level privilege |
| Max duration | `TMR-11-BYPMAX`, auto-expiry |
| Indication | Bypass-active alarm (priority medium), shown on bypass summary display, event logged |
| Procedure | Bypass permit per site procedure. Operator continuously monitors local gauge PI-1105A. |

### 10. Alarms and HMI
| Alarm / indication | Tag.attribute | Setpoint ref | Priority | Display |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fuel gas pressure low (pre-alarm) | PT-1105.LO | `SPR-1105-L` | Medium | H-110 graphic, alarm list |
| Fuel gas pressure LL trip | IL-11-007.TRIP | `SPR-1105-LL` | High | First-out FO-11-H110 |
| XV-1106 discrepancy | XV-1106.DISC | `TMR-1106-TRV` | High | Faceplate |
| Bypass active | IL-11-007.BYP | — | Medium | Bypass summary |

### 11. Fault handling
- **PT-1105 bad quality** (open circuit, out of range, HART fault): trip after delay, per section 5.
- **AI card failure:** same as bad quality.
- **Controller failover:** trip state and latch are retained across switchover. Verify at FAT.
- **XV-1106 output card failure:** SOV de-energizes, so the valve closes (fail-safe).

### 12. Test basis (FAT)
**Preconditions:** PT-1105 simulated at normal operating pressure. XV-1106 feedback simulated open. Interlock reset. No bypass or startup override active. Register extract printed and revision recorded.

| Step | Action | Expected result | Value source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Ramp PT-1105 to just above LL | No trip. Low pre-alarm active below L. | `SPR-1105-L`, `SPR-1105-LL` |
| 2 | Drop PT-1105 below LL for less than the delay, then restore | No trip | `TMR-1105-LL` |
| 3 | Drop PT-1105 below LL and hold | Trip at delay ±1 scan. XV-1106 DO de-energized. FV-1107 to MAN at min output. LL alarm raised. First-out shows IL-11-007. | `TMR-1105-LL`, `SPR-1107-MINOP` |
| 4 | Withhold ZSC-1106 feedback | Discrepancy alarm after travel time | `TMR-1106-TRV` |
| 5 | Operator attempts to open XV-1106 | Command rejected | — |
| 6 | Raise PT-1105 above LL but below RST, press reset | Reset rejected | `SPR-1105-RST` |
| 7 | Raise PT-1105 above RST, press reset | Reset accepted. XV-1106 remains closed. | `SPR-1105-RST` |
| 8 | Operator opens XV-1106 with PT-1105 low | Startup override active. No trip until timer expires, then trip. | `TMR-1105-SUO` |
| 9 | Repeat step 8 but raise PT-1105 above RST before expiry | Override cancels early. Interlock armed. | `SPR-1105-RST` |
| 10 | Set PT-1105 to bad quality (simulate open circuit) | Trip after delay | `TMR-1105-LL` |
| 11 | Apply maintenance bypass at operator level, then at engineer level | Operator attempt rejected. Engineer bypass accepted, alarmed and logged. Expires after max duration. | `TMR-11-BYPMAX` |
| 12 | With trip active, force controller switchover | Trip and latch retained | — |
| 13 | Compare configured parameters to register extract | All match | Register rev __ |

**Tolerance:** analog trip within ±0.5% of span. Timers within ±1 scan.

### 13. Open items
| # | Item | Owner | Due |
|---|---|---|---|
| OI-1 | Resolve LL setpoint (C&E 0.35 vs logic 0.30 barg) and enter it in register | Process eng. | |
| OI-2 | Confirm bad-PV action is trip | Process / Ops | |
| OI-3 | Confirm FV-1107 action from legacy sheet 41 | Control sys. | |
| OI-4 | Confirm classification against SRS and BMS scope | Process safety | |

### 14. Approval
*(blank)*

---

**Illustrative register rows** (these live in the register, not on the IDS):

| ID | Tag.attribute | Value | Units | Basis | Rev / MOC |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SPR-1105-L | PT-1105.LO | 0.50 | barg | Burner vendor data | 0 |
| SPR-1105-LL | PT-1105.LL | *TBD (OI-1)* | barg | Burner min stable pressure | — |
| SPR-1105-RST | IL-11-007.RST | LL + 0.10 | barg | Deadband | 0 |
| TMR-1105-LL | IL-11-007.DLY | 2 | s | Legacy | 0 |
| TMR-1105-SUO | IL-11-007.SUO | 30 | s | Light-off procedure | 0 |
| TMR-1106-TRV | XV-1106.TRV | 10 | s | Valve datasheet | 0 |

## Notes for the migration

- **Check the classification of this particular example.** On many fired heaters, low fuel gas pressure to main-fuel shut-off is a BMS or SIS function under API 556 or your site's BMS standard, not BPCS. Section 1 exists to catch this. If XV-1106 is also a SIF final element, the BPCS should normally act through its own SOV or a separate valve, and that arrangement needs to be explicit in the sheet.
- **Expect discrepancies like the one in OI-1.** Across 40 units, you will find many cases where the C&E and the logic disagree. Section 3 gives each discrepancy a home, and the register forces a single resolution.
- **Generate the FAT procedure from section 12.** If you hold the IDS as structured data (a spreadsheet or database with one row per cause or effect), you can generate the procedure automatically, with register values merged in at print time. That gives you requirement (b) almost for free.
- **Use a trip summary sheet per heater or unit** (like IDS-11-010) to list all its interlocks and first-out groups. This keeps the overall picture visible without repeating any detail.
